gaps.title: Independent proof of career record and technical leadership
gaps.what_is_missing: The public profile makes broad claims about over 20 years of IT expertise and technical leadership, but the ledger identifies these as self-stated rather than independently confirmed. Claims about building data platforms and architecting DevOps and MLOps solutions are also not supported here by named projects, employer confirmation, customer references, or measurable outcomes.
gaps.why_it_matters: Investors, enterprise clients, and journalists need to distinguish a personal bio from a documented professional record. Without third-party evidence, it is difficult to assess seniority, scope of responsibility, and delivered technical impact.
gaps.fix: Publish a concise career record with verifiable employers, roles, dates, selected projects, and references or case studies that can independently confirm the work.

gaps.title: Community traction is presented without independent validation
gaps.what_is_missing: The profile cites a DataOps meetup community with 2350+ members and a LinkedIn page with around 1300+ followers, but both figures are treated as self-reported in the ledger. Other activity and engagement claims also remain unverified, leaving no clear public trail of event archives, attendee evidence, partner organizations, or community outcomes.
gaps.why_it_matters: Audience size alone does not establish an active or influential community. A serious counterparty will want proof of engagement, repeat participation, speaker quality, and the practical value created for members.
gaps.fix: Maintain public event pages and a periodic community report that links to agendas, speakers, attendance evidence, recordings, partner acknowledgements, and current platform metrics.

gaps.title: High-profile affiliations and recognitions are not clearly substantiated
gaps.what_is_missing: The ledger does not independently verify public claims connecting Ayyanar Jeyakrishnan with an AWS Machine Learning Hero designation, a senior role at Wells Fargo, AzConf, or a Microsoft Build event. The public-facing material needs direct, authoritative links and a clear explanation of what each affiliation, recognition, or speaking role involved.
gaps.why_it_matters: Recognitions and major-company affiliations can materially shape credibility, so ambiguity creates avoidable diligence risk. If a claim cannot be readily confirmed from an authoritative record, readers may question the accuracy of the wider profile.
gaps.fix: Create a verified media and credentials page linking directly to authoritative organizer, employer, and program records, with a short description of each role or recognition.
